acceptance: A stand-in posted after failing review-event runs lets the pull request merge after one documented action, without re-running each stale run by hand
Either the check is reported once per head (later runs supersede earlier ones), or review-event runs no longer leave failing check runs on the head
docs/operations/soundness-drain.md states the recovery that actually works
A test or recorded CI evidence covers the stale-failure case
context: Related: oracle-review-thread-reply-run-churn-20261008 (runs per thread reply). Stale runs on #2784: 37852065358, 37852876606, 37854418822.
description: On #2784 (head 8eb562e01) every required check passed and a fresh pull_request (reopened) oracle-review run succeeded after the stand-in, yet the pull request stayed BLOCKED. Earlier oracle-review runs started by pull_request_review (submitted) events, before the stand-in existed, had concluded failure and still counted. Merging needed each stale run re-run one at a time: parallel `gh run rerun` calls cancel each other through the oracle-review-<pr> concurrency group. #2769 showed the same symptom. The documented recovery (close/reopen) is not enough on its own, and it restarts the whole CI suite.
